newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan's Crown Prince snubs Israel over water row.
newsitem.headline: Jordan's Crown Prince snubs Israel over water row.

text.p: Jordan said on Tuesday it had called off a meeting between Crown Prince Hassan and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu over disagreements about Jordan's water supplies set out in their 1994 peace treaty.

Information Minister Samir Mutawae said the prince and the prime minister had been due to hold talks during a ceremony in memory of seven Israeli girls killed by a Jordanian soldier near their joint border in March.

But he said Israel backed down from an understanding that it would sign an accord covering an extra 50 million cubic metres of water a year which Israel pledged under the peace treaty to help Jordan, facing major water shortages, to obtain.
Israel said on Tuesday it was cancelling the whole memorial ceremony in the wake of Prince Hassan's decision to stay away.
"This subject of providing the 50 million cubic metres (of water) was discussed several times in the past years," Mutawae told Reuters.
"The Israelis responded by showing readiness to provide the quantity from their sources and (showed) understanding of Jordan's need to build dams and other collecting facilities."

The treaty signed by the two countries, which ended a 46-year state of war, specifies that within one year of its coming into force in November 1994 the two sides would develop a plan to supply Jordan with the water.
No such plan was formally implemented.

Foreign Minister Fayez al-Tarawneh spoke earlier this week of a "frustration in the whole peace process" and said Israel's failure to follow up its commitment to supply water to Jordan was a breach of the 1994 treaty.
Mutawae said Jordan thought that "a provision" for the 50 million cubic metres could be signed at the same time as the memorial ceremony for the seven Israeli schoolgirls.
"At the last minute they said they wanted the cabinet to discuss it and they were not ready to sign it," he added.

Instead of meeting Netanyahu, Prince Hassan on Tuesday held talks with Israeli Labour Party member Yossi Beilin, an architect of the troubled Palestinian self-rule agreement agreed with Israel in 1993.

Beilin was also due to meet Tarawneh and Prime Minister Abdul-Salam al-Majali. He is pushing an initiative to restart Israel-Palestinian peace talks but Netanyahu's spokesmen say Beilin has no authority to conduct negotiations for Israel and Jordanian officials have not commented on the talks.

The ceremony in memory of the March 13 killing was to have been held at a beauty spot on Jordanian soil leased to Israeli farmers under the peace treaty. Israel calls the area Naharayim as well as the Island of Peace. It is called Baqoura in Jordan.
The girls' parents were to dedicate a "hill of flowers" and plant trees at the site on Tuesday.
Jordan's King Hussein paid a condolence call on the victims' families after the attack and expressed shame at the massacre.

Netanyahu's media adviser David Bar-Illan had told Israel Radio on Monday issues to be discussed at the meeting included building a joint airport on the Red Sea, diverting Jordan River water to Jordan, tourism projects at the Dead Sea and other industry and trade issues.
